title: Adapting Job Recommendations to User Preference Drift with Behavioral-Semantic Fusion Learning

problem.claim: Job recommendation systems need to align job opportunities with job-seekers while capturing user preferences that change during job seeking.

gap.claim: Frequent preference drift makes it difficult for existing job recommendation approaches to capture user preferences promptly and precisely, limiting recommendation performance.

contributions.claim: BISTRO is a session-based framework that models user preference through fusion learning of semantic and behavioral information.
BISTRO combines coarse-grained semantic clustering, fine-grained job preference extraction, and personalized top-k job recommendation.
BISTRO uses hypergraph wavelet learning, adaptive wavelet filtering, and a recurrent neural network to capture preference drift, reduce interaction noise, and infer personalized preferences.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present BISTRO as a novel session-based framework and describe the adaptive wavelet filtering technique as innovative.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on three real-world offline recruitment datasets reportedly demonstrate significant performance for BISTRO.
Online experiments reportedly show that BISTRO is effective in live recruitment settings.
The authors characterize the combined offline and online results as evidence of robustness and adaptability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Job recommender systems align job opportunities with job-seekers.
Continually changing user preferences and frequent preference drift limit recommendation performance and make timely, precise preference capture difficult.
BISTRO addresses the problem with a three-stage session-based framework using semantic and behavioral fusion, clustering, preference extraction, filtering, and recurrent modeling.
The authors report strong results in offline experiments across three recruitment datasets and in online recruitment experiments.
The authors interpret the offline and online results as indicating robustness and adaptability.
